title: A Body Prepared — EA-ARK-FICTION-01
creator: Lee Sharks
description: Yehonatan, sixteen years old, did not yet know this. He knew only that the workshop smelled of olive-oil smoke and dry ink, and of something else underneath -- a thread of iron, like the well-water at his mother's house when he was small. He knew that the Teacher slept only in the hours before dawn, and that the frame in the rear chamber was draped always in coarse cloth, and that the women who came at dusk to bring the oils and the spices did not speak to the scribes, and the scribes did not speak to them, but bowed when they passed each other in the narrow limestone corridor. He knew the order of his tasks. He knew the recipe for the ink: gall of the oak, iron sulfate from the Samaritan hills, gum of the acacia, a little wine to loosen it, a grain of myrrh to keep the worms out. He could grind pigment without spilling it. He could trim a reed pen. He could copy a line of the _Hodayot_ without his hand trembling. For these things he was permitted to sit among the scribes, and to listen, and sometimes to understand. The scribes debated in low voices across the long stone table. They argued about scars. They argued about whether a particular verse should say _pierced_ or _drawn through_. They argued about the arrangement of the stripes on a back -- whether Roman flagella made marks in threes or in pairs or in the long unbroken diagonals the Greek sources described, and which mat.

wiki_article:
**A Body Prepared — EA-ARK-FICTION-01** is a work of creative prose by Lee Sharks, deposited 18 April 2026 at 26,186 characters — the Ark fiction series' principal narrative.

It opens in close third person on a boy in a workshop: *"Yehonatan, sixteen years old, did not yet know this. He knew only that the workshop smelled of olive-oil smoke and dry ink, and of something else underneath — a thread of iron, like the well-water at his mother's house."* The sensory register is doing theological work — olive oil, ink and iron are the materials of anointing, scripture and nails.

Its title comes from Hebrews 10:5, *"a body thou hast prepared me,"* which is itself a quotation of the Septuagint's rendering of Psalm 40 — a text whose transmission history is a substitution. The compressed companion, *Homunculus*, is deposited separately at **#1354** on the archive's principle that a compression is a distinct object rather than a summary.
